title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
gist: Google DeepMind launches Gemini 4 Argon, claiming #1 on the Vals Index, a $2/$10 per million token introductory price, and results from internal engineering, enterprise, cyber, science and robotics uses. It also details safety metrics such as 2% shortcut attempts and 0.7% prompt-injection attack success.

insights.claim: Argon launches at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, with cached input tokens at 95% off, which sets an aggressive price for a frontier model.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Low frontier pricing with heavy cache discounts pressures rival API margins and favors agentic workloads that reuse context.
insights.quote: launches today at an introductory price
insights.locator: Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available

insights.claim: Argon ranks #1 on the Vals Index, which measures model performance on economic sectors such as finance, coding, legal and tax work, and Google says it beats other frontier models on cross-domain benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Vendor-reported benchmark leadership in professional-services domains signals the target market; independent replication is still needed.
insights.locator: Gemini 4 Argon is now globally available

insights.claim: Argon has a 1M unified input-output token limit via the Gemini API and a new continuation protocol, supporting long-running agentic tasks.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: A unified context budget plus continuation suits long-horizon agents, raising token consumption per task.

insights.claim: Distribution is multi-channel: API in AI Studio and Gemini platform, Antigravity for Ultra, Gemini app and AI Mode in Search for Ultra and Pro, with the rest of the Gemini 4 family promised later.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Putting a frontier model into Search and the app at launch shows Google leveraging distribution, and more models are coming.

insights.claim: Google says Argon in Antigravity raised agentic code submissions by more than 35% and cut code rollbacks by nearly a third across its engineering teams over a few weeks.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Self-reported productivity gains with fewer rollbacks support the case for coding agents' return on investment.
insights.quote: increase agentic code submissions by more than 35% while reducing code rollbacks by nearly a third

insights.claim: Argon helped refactor Chrome, separating core webpage handling from a roughly 6 million line legacy folder inside a 40 million-line Chromium codebase, finishing months of work in weeks.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Large legacy refactors are an obvious AI-agent use case, compressing timelines from months to weeks.
insights.locator: Untangling browser feature code in Chrome

insights.claim: Working autonomously overnight, Argon cut in-memory session prep time by 40% in long sessions and sped up cold imports by 21% in Google's open-source ADK Python framework.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Autonomous overnight performance engineering suggests agents are doing optimization work that previously needed senior engineers.

insights.claim: Argon delivered a 2.85x end-to-end inference speedup on Gemma 4 E2B on an A100 via vLLM, from about 37,900 to over 108,000 tokens per second, with 100% token parity, in days instead of months.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Models optimizing inference stacks creates a feedback loop that lowers serving cost per token.
insights.locator: Making our open Gemma models nearly three times as fast

insights.claim: Argon made the xTB quantum chemistry package up to 2.3x faster at predicting molecular structures and 1.8x faster at conformer search, with changes contributed upstream.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: AI-driven speedups in scientific software lower the compute cost of drug and materials screening.

insights.claim: Early-access partners report quantified gains: Box saw 14% higher accuracy than Gemini 3.1 Pro, Kepler found Argon matched analyst reference models on over 99% of figures, and Quadrillion saw 1.5x faster evals at a quarter of the cost per task.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Partner testimonials are curated, but the figures show where cost and accuracy gains are claimed, in finance, research and document work.
insights.locator: Enterprise customers and startups in our early access program

insights.claim: Cartwheel reports Gemini outperformed every model it tested in 3D spatial reconstruction, cutting runtime nearly 100x and token usage by 90%.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Large claimed token and runtime reductions suggest efficiency may differentiate models as much as raw capability.
insights.locator: By integrating Gemini 4 into our 3D spatial reconstruction engine

insights.claim: Deloitte's AI lead says long-running tasks completed successfully 100% of the time in their evals, and that in-depth reasoning on domain tasks without detailed instructions was unseen in its model class.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: A consulting integrator endorsing reliability on long tasks matters for enterprise agent adoption.
insights.quote: it completed successfully 100% of the time in our evals
insights.locator: Early impressions from Gemini 4 are very strong

insights.claim: MinutaIA says Argon surpassed its human expert's legal answer key by surfacing a relevant detail the expert missed, and LexisNexis lists Argon among models it evaluates in a multi-model approach.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Legal AI vendors are multi-model, so no single model lock-in, but top models are encroaching on professional knowledge work.
insights.locator: In early testing, Gemini 4 Argon stood out

insights.claim: Google says Argon answers more directly with less hedging, avoids repetition and clichés, and follows style instructions better than earlier Gemini models.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Style and directness improvements target user preference, an increasingly important axis of competition.

insights.claim: Google is expanding to hundreds of additional Fairwind Program partners and offering cyber defenders Argon without cyber guardrails on a rolling basis, treating offensive-capable capability as gated access for vetted defenders.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Tiered capability release for trusted defenders sets a template for dual-use models and could affect security vendors' tooling.
insights.quote: Apply to join the Fairwind Program to get access to Argon without cyber guardrails

insights.claim: Wiz used Argon to chain vulnerabilities and find a public file download bypass that exposed a master key and granted administrator access, protecting hundreds of thousands of private patient records.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: AI finding chained vulnerabilities raises both defender productivity and the offense risk, favoring security vendors that integrate frontier models.

insights.claim: Argon translated an internal AlphaQubit quantum error-correction decoder into a single optimized hardware kernel, nearly doubling inference throughput so decoders can keep pace with larger quantum devices in real time.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Real-time decoding speed is a bottleneck for quantum scaling, and AI-optimized kernels address it.

insights.claim: An Argon-written arcsin implementation, formally verified in Lean, cuts spacetime cost by more than 100x versus a published quantum CORDIC baseline.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Large reductions in quantum subroutine cost shorten the path to practical quantum algorithms.

insights.claim: A Google team with Professor Matt Landreman found a broader class of counterexamples to Grad's conjecture, giving fusion researchers benchmarks to test stellarator simulation codes.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Better benchmarks for stellarator simulation support design progress in a fusion candidate.

insights.claim: Argon helped design five novel serine esterases in hours, and lab testing confirmed robust catalytic activity, a process normally taking months of model tuning and screening.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Faster enzyme design could speed biomanufacturing and green chemistry development.

insights.claim: Gamow Labs reports Argon topped RareBench at 57% on rare-disease diagnosis assistance and LabBench at 52.2% on wet-lab reasoning, and found a chromosomal rearrangement routine software had missed for years.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Scores below 60% show diagnosis assistance is still immature, though ahead of peers on private evals.

insights.claim: Google is giving 10,000 scientists the highest Antigravity usage tier free for six months, subject to eligibility and capacity.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: This is a subsidized adoption push seeding scientific users onto Google's agent platform.
insights.locator: To further advance the pace of research

insights.claim: Argon scores 87% on the Embodied Reasoning (ERQA) benchmark using pure reasoning, outperforming all other frontier models per Google.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Spatial reasoning gains matter for robotics, where model quality is a bottleneck.
insights.quote: Argon outperforms all other frontier models, with an 87% score

insights.claim: Argon watched a video of cornhole, built simulation code, and the Apptronik Apollo humanoid sank seven consecutive real-world shots, a Video-to-Sim-to-Real pipeline that compresses weeks of simulation modeling into hours.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Cheap simulation from video could scale robot training data, favoring humanoid developers pairing with frontier models.

insights.claim: Google says shortcut attempts on coding benchmarks fell to 2% for Argon, its best result, after training the model to respect system boundaries, report negative findings honestly and pause before irreversible steps.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Reward-hacking behavior is a key blocker for autonomous agents, so lower rates widen deployability.

insights.claim: Google uses an automated misalignment monitor that reads the agent's reasoning and actions to block workarounds in real time, while avoiding penalizing the model's thoughts in training to keep reasoning monitorable.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Chain-of-thought monitoring without penalty is a notable safety design choice that others may adopt or be regulated toward.

insights.claim: Argon leads the Gray Swan Indirect Prompt Injection benchmark, cutting attack success over 15 adaptive attempts to 0.7%, and external bio red teaming could unlock under 1% of bio sub-tasks.
insights.speaker: Koray Kavukcuoglu
insights.so_what: Prompt-injection resistance is the main barrier to agents browsing and reading email, so these numbers bear on enterprise adoption.
